target: More World Bank RAMP members (priority one)
searched: World Bank press-release channel in English, Spanish and French: "joins World Bank RAMP", "Reserves Advisory and Management Partnership" with years 2023-2026, "se une a RAMP", "adhere au RAMP", plus country-specific queries (Uzbekistan, Nepal, Mongolia, Albania, North Macedonia, Mauritius, Uganda, Rwanda, Zambia, Georgia, Somalia)
outcome: The worldbank.org press-release vein appears exhausted: every announcement returned was for a bank already held (Bosnia, Armenia, Liberia, Ecuador, Kosovo, Zimbabwe, Cabo Verde, Paraguay, Libya) or for a non-central-bank member (Pension Agency of Georgia, Turkic Investment Fund). Two new central banks were found from their OWN publications rather than the World Bank: Somalia (CBS 2024 Newsletter) and Georgia (NBG news item). A Somali National News Agency page that matched RAMP searches turned out to contain no RAMP content.
next_step: Stop searching worldbank.org. Mine central banks' own newsletters, annual reports and governor statements for the phrase "RAMP" one country at a time; the Somalia and Georgia hits both came that way. Pension funds and sovereign funds are also RAMP members and have their own announcements.

searched: Bank of Mauritius Annual Report 2025, Bank of Papua New Guinea Annual Report 2024, Central Bank of Iceland international reserves page, Bank of Sierra Leone Financial Statements 2024, Eastern Caribbean Central Bank audited financial statements to 31 March 2025, Czech National Bank quarterly international reserves information, Bank of Uganda Auditor General's Report 2024
outcome: One rich hit: BPNG's annual report names Pictet, DWS and BlackRock as external managers of its reserves. Bank of Sierra Leone names no manager but does state that its Stabilization and Cooperation Fund contribution is managed by the West African Monetary Institute and held at the Bank of Ghana. ECCB refers to "external fund managers", "asset managers" and "the global custodian" generically across both halves of its financial statements and names none. CNB says only that "The mandate of the external managers responsible for MBS investments was terminated in 2026 Q3" without naming them. Bank of Mauritius's 2025 report (first 100k characters) names no external manager and describes an in-house framework. Iceland's cb.is reserves page returned no body text. The Bank of Uganda Auditor General PDF URL returned only a help-desk shell.
next_step: Mauritius remains unresolved past character 100,000 of its 474,000-character report; same for BPNG past 100,000 and ECCB past 200,000. Untried from the priority list: Namibia, Rwanda, Kenya, Zambia, Nepal, Mongolia, North Macedonia, Albania, Barbados, Malta, Cyprus. Bank of Tanzania's PDFs are on a server that rejects fetches.

target: Managers' and custodians' own disclosures (priority three)
searched: Central Banking awards profiles for Crown Agents Investment Management, Amundi, Invesco, State Street Global Advisors, BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, HSBC (asset services and global markets), Northern Trust and BNY Mellon; plus the 2026 first-winners announcement
outcome: This was by far the richest vein and centralbanking.com pages fetch without a hard paywall on the opening sections. Named pairings found: CAIM with Eswatini, Solomon Islands and Jamaica; Amundi with Colombia; SSGA with the Czech National Bank; BlackRock with Israel and Lithuania; Northern Trust with Botswana and Uganda; BNY Mellon with Cambodia; Amundi and FLAR with Uruguay and Mexico. Two of these contradict earlier dead-end findings in a useful way: Bank of Israel, recorded as naming no one itself, is named by BlackRock's profile, and Bank of Botswana, which names no firm in its own disclosures, is named by Northern Trust's profile. Invesco's profile describes an "undisclosed central bank"; Franklin Templeton's is cut off by the paywall after stating it manages around 26 billion US dollars for central banks; HSBC's asset services profile names countries but no central bank client.
next_step: Work through the remaining Central Banking awards years systematically - 2017, 2019-2024 asset manager, global custodian, asset services provider and partner initiative categories each tend to name one or two clients. The 2026 announcement says further tranches of winners followed, so later 2026 profiles are unread. Also unread: the dedicated Amundi-FLAR partner initiative profile, and the Franklin Templeton profile beyond the paywall.

target: Firms whose relationship is stated but not as management
searched: HSBC global markets award, CNB quarterly reserves information, SimCorp at the Central Bank of Sri Lanka
outcome: Deliberately not recorded. HSBC's 2018 award was for "organising financing to bolster the foreign exchange reserves of the Central Bank of Egypt", which is arranging financing rather than managing, advising on or holding reserves. SimCorp at Sri Lanka is a software vendor. Both fail the relation test.
next_step: If the map later wants a financing or systems-vendor relation, Egypt-HSBC and Sri Lanka-SimCorp are already located.
